newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks pause after big surge.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks pause after big surge.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks moved lower on profit taking Wednesday, one day after a rush of buying in big-name shares lifted the Dow Jones industrial average to its second largest daily gain ever.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was off 4.41 points at 6,829.18. On Tuesday, the index jumped 173 points, which was second in point terms only to the 187-point leap that came two days after the "Black Monday" stock market crash of Oct. 19, 1987.
High technology stocks, however, extended Tuesday's rally, lifting the Nasdaq Composite index 11.39 points to 1,224.13.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of 281 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The fact that we had no big followthrough (on the Dow) points out that yesterday was a fluke, in the sense that there was a brief panic into defensive stocks by portfolio managers. The rest of the market did not do that much," said Phil Roth, chief technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds.
Tuesday's rally was concentrated in a handful of blue-chip stocks and was a boon for the Dow.

Alfred Goldman, analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons, said, "My gut feeling is that we had a buying climax yesterday. The rally yesterday was of poor quality. Volume, breadth, new highs and new lows were all poor."
The weakness in the Dow came in spite of a jump in the shares of International Business Machines Corp., which is expected to report first quarter earnings after the closing bell.
IBM was up 1-1/2 at 141-1/2 after having gone as high as 143-1/4 in early trading.

Other high techs also put in a strong showing. Microsoft Corp. was up 3 at 113-5/8, Intel Corp. rose 3 to 143-7/8 and PeopleSoft Inc., which said it expected total revenues in 1997 to be up 70 percent, was up 6-1/16 at 41-1/16.

"The high techs started a deep oversold rally yesterday and it could go on for another hour, or for a day and an hour. then they will slip back down," Goldman said. "It would be presumptuous to say that the techs have bottomed."

Among special situations, Planet Hollywood International Inc. gained 2-3/8 at 18-1/2. Planet Hollywood and Saudi Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud said they formed an alliance that calls for the prince to develop up to 34 Planet restaurants in 23 countries.
Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc. lost 4-3/8 at 30-1/2. The giant U.S.-Swedish pharmaceutical group, issued a surprise profit warning, sending the company's share price plummeting.
